grammar_points.name: Verb 'be' - affirmative
grammar_points.explanation: Affirmative contracted forms of 'be' used to state facts about people and places: I'm, He's/She's/It's, We're/You're/They're (e.g. 'I'm from Kamakura.', 'It's an old city.', 'We're from Australia.').

grammar_points.name: Verb 'be' - negative
grammar_points.explanation: Negative contracted forms of 'be': I'm not, He isn't/She isn't/It isn't, We aren't/You aren't/They aren't (e.g. 'I'm not British.', 'It isn't famous.', 'We aren't American.').

grammar_points.name: Nationality adjective formation
grammar_points.explanation: Most nationality adjectives are formed by adding -an, -ish, or -ese to (a form of) the country name (e.g. Canada -> Canadian, Turkey -> Turkish, Japan -> Japanese). Some are irregular (e.g. France -> French, Switzerland -> Swiss, Czech Republic -> Czech).
